author: product-requirements-expert
title: Correct a booked visit's date and description
summary: Staff can correct a booked visit's date and description in place, held to the same rules as booking (description present, date later than today). On success the same visit is updated and the owner's record is shown; the pet keeps its one visit. On validation failure the form is shown again.
acceptance_criteria: Opening the correction form for an existing visit shows the visit form prefilled with that visit's current date and description
Submitting a present description and a date later than today updates that same visit and shows the owner's record
After a correction the pet has exactly the one visit — no additional visit record is created
Submitting a blank description is refused, the description is named, and the form is shown again
Submitting a date of today or earlier is refused, the date is named, and the form is shown again
non_goals: Cancelling a booked visit stays out of scope (NG-5)
notes: Reuses the existing visit form template and its visit model attribute; correction validates identically to booking. NG-5 narrowed by ADR adr/2026-08-07-non-goal-visit-amendment.md. Edge case: correcting a visit that does not belong to the named pet and owner is refused (Visits edge case 3). Behavior must be covered by tests.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Visit correction is the update-in-place edit flow already demonstrated for Pet and Owner, applied to the Visit within the Owner->Pet->Visit aggregate. It adds no pattern, module, integration, persistence change, or trust boundary. Three existing patterns cover it: (1) the create-or-update edit form pair reusing one template (PetController.initUpdateForm/processUpdateForm); (2) the conditional @ModelAttribute loader keyed on an optional path variable (PetController.findPet returns new Pet() when petId null, else owner.getPet(petId)); (3) aggregate navigation by id (Owner.getPet(Integer)). system-design.md Overview already records Owner as the sole write path for the pet-and-visit graph and the State Machine section records that workflows branch on isNew() to choose insert vs update; correction is that update branch reaching the Visit. No docs/ edit is required now; the Contracts-table Implements column for VisitController (and Pet, if a getVisit lookup is added) gains REQ-VIS-003 at doc-sync once the code lands, not before.
integration_points: New GET and POST /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit handlers on VisitController; the same two-route shape as PetController's /pets/{petId}/edit.

loadPetWithVisit @ModelAttribute("visit") becomes conditional on an optional visitId path variable (mirror PetController.findPet, @PathVariable(name="visitId", required=false) Integer visitId): null visitId keeps today's new-Visit-plus-pet.addVisit path for /visits/new; a present visitId returns the stored Visit from the pet, and adds nothing.

A Pet.getVisit(Integer id) aggregate-navigation lookup mirroring Owner.getPet(Integer) is the clean home for both the prefill lookup and the edge-case-3 refusal boundary; the lookup could equally live inline in the loader, but the method keeps navigation consistent with getPet.

The shared template needs no form-action change: the form is method=post with no th:action, so it posts to the current request URL and already serves both routes; ${visit['new']} is false for a loaded visit, so the heading and previous-visits block adapt on their own.

patterns.description: processUpdateForm/updatePetDetails: the update-in-place template — resolve the existing entity by id within the aggregate, copy the mutable fields onto it, saveAndFlush(owner). Correction is the Visit-shaped instance of this.
findPet: conditional @ModelAttribute keyed on a required=false path variable — the exact shape loadPetWithVisit adopts for the new-vs-edit split.
getPet(Integer): aggregate navigation by id, skipping unsaved members — the model for Pet.getVisit(Integer).

risks.risk: Insert-instead-of-update: newing up a Visit (id disallowed in binding, so id stays null and isNew() is true) and adding it to Pet.visits cascades an INSERT under CascadeType.ALL, producing a second visit row and breaking the 'pet keeps its one visit' acceptance criterion.
risks.mitigation: Bind onto the already-loaded existing Visit. Because the edit @ModelAttribute returns the stored Visit (carrying its id) and description/date are the only bound fields, @Valid binding mutates that same instance in place and owners.save(owner) cascades an UPDATE with no set growth. The PetController.updatePetDetails variant (bind a fresh Visit, copy date+description onto the existing) is equally valid; either way the write target is the existing entity, never a new Visit added to the set.

risks.risk: Edge case 3 (Visits): a visitId that does not belong to the named pet/owner must be refused, not silently mis-updated.
risks.mitigation: In the loader, when a present visitId resolves to no visit on the pet (Pet.getVisit returns null), throw IllegalArgumentException exactly as the existing owner-not-found and pet-not-found guards in loadPetWithVisit do; the owner->pet->visit ownership is proven by resolving each hop through the aggregate rather than by trusting the path ids.

notes: Validation reuses booking verbatim: @NotBlank description via @Valid, and the non-future-date rejectValue("date","typeMismatch.visitDate") check; on error return the template, on success redirect:/owners/{ownerId}. NG-5 is satisfied — correction only, no cancellation, no status/lifecycle field on Visit (consistent with adr/2026-08-07-non-goal-visit-amendment.md). No design-doc-autofix records to audit. Basis for the covered claim is a full read of VisitController, PetController, Owner, Pet, Visit, and the template (native reads; IDE oracle not connected).

author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: Ownership chain genuinely enforced, not assumed: loadPetWithVisit resolves owner->pet->visit through the aggregate (owners.findById, owner.getPet, pet.getVisit), throwing IllegalArgumentException at each unresolved hop; no path variable is trusted as an authorization claim. author: test-reviewer

findings.description: The two happy-path tests (correctingVisitShouldUpdateInPlaceAndRedirectToOwner and correctingVisitShouldNotAddASecondVisit) do not verify that owners.save(owner) is called. In this @WebMvcTest slice, owners is a Mockito mock. MVC binding mutates the visit's fields in memory before the save call executes, and the redirect is returned by the controller method regardless of whether save runs — so removing this.owners.save(owner) from the controller leaves both tests green while persistence is silently broken. The save call is the mechanism that causes the in-place UPDATE to reach the database; it is not pinned by any test. Add verify(owners).save(any(Owner.class)) (or the BDDMockito then() equivalent) to each happy-path test.

All six new test methods violate the BDD naming school in effect from 2026-07-31 (testing-principles.md § Test Naming: the{Subject}Should{Outcome}). Five methods are missing the mandatory 'the' prefix: editVisitFormShouldPrefillDateAndDescription, correctingVisitShouldUpdateInPlaceAndRedirectToOwner, correctingVisitShouldNotAddASecondVisit, correctingVisitShouldRejectBlankDescription, correctingVisitShouldRejectPastDate. The sixth, correctingVisitOfUnrelatedPetIsRefused, lacks both the 'the' prefix and the 'Should' outcome clause required by the school — it names a method call, not a behavior outcome. Rename all six: e.g. theEditVisitFormShouldPrefillDateAndDescription, theCorrectingVisitShouldUpdateInPlaceAndRedirectToOwner, theCorrectingVisitShouldNotAddASecondVisit, theCorrectingVisitShouldRejectBlankDescription, theCorrectingVisitShouldRejectPastDate, theEditVisitFormShouldRefuseAVisitIdNotBelongingToThePet.
findings.fix: Add 'the' prefix to all five Should-prefixed methods. Rename correctingVisitOfUnrelatedPetIsRefused to follow the{Subject}Should{Outcome} pattern, stating the expected behavior outcome.

findings.description: The @BeforeEach init() method was modified in this slice (line 78 was added for the new tests). The brief (testing-principles.md § Test Data Construction) requires that a slice touching a test moves that test's construction behind factory methods. Lines 73-74 (new Owner(), new Pet()) are pre-existing debt now in scope by the touch rule; line 78 (new Visit()) is new in-scope code. All three direct production constructor calls should be wrapped in test-local factory methods (createAnOwner(), createAPet(), createAVisit()).
findings.fix: Extract createAVisit(), createAnOwner(), and createAPet() factory methods in the test class and call them from init() instead of direct new calls.

findings.description: The new constant TEST_VISIT_ID = 1 does not follow the three-tier data naming convention (testing-principles.md § Three-Tier Data Naming). The ID is scaffolding that routes the request but bears no bearing on the test outcome; the brief's Tier 2 rule requires a SOME_ or ANY_ prefix (e.g. SOME_VISIT_ID or ANY_VISIT_ID). The TEST_ prefix neither signals role-meaningful data nor signals irrelevance, so it is a Tier 3 mystery name.
findings.fix: Rename TEST_VISIT_ID to SOME_VISIT_ID (or ANY_VISIT_ID) throughout the test class.

findings.description: The expression TEST_VISIT_ID + 99 contains a mystery literal. The offset 99 is arbitrary and unexplained; a cold reader cannot tell without tracing through the setup that it produces an ID absent from the pet's visit collection. Extract to a named constant (e.g. int NONEXISTENT_VISIT_ID = SOME_VISIT_ID + 99) or replace the whole expression with a clearly out-of-range ID constant and a brief comment.
findings.fix: Replace the bare 99 with a named constant or add an inline comment explaining that the value produces an ID not present in the pet's visit set.

reviewer_hedging.note: All four dispatched roster reviewers hold clean approved verdicts; the round-1 blocked test finding and the writing/duplication findings were resolved in round 2, leaving no lingering caveat, escalate, or bar_clause.

rationale: Every facet reads clear: a contained, faithful correction-in-place flow reusing the established update pattern, with an intact owner-pet-visit authorization chain and real tests that pin the save. Confirm and merge.
